weight_note: For certifications whose public overview page does not expose detailed exam-domain percentages in machine-readable page content, weights below are normalized curriculum planning weights across Snowflake's published certification capability areas. They are not represented as official exam-domain percentages.

skills.title: Navigate Snowsight and core Snowflake interfaces
skills.objective: Use Snowflake interfaces to locate databases, worksheets, monitoring views, and administrative areas.
exam_traps: Confusing interface navigation with account-level privileges.

skills.title: Use Snowflake Notebooks for interactive analysis
skills.objective: Recognize Snowflake Notebook concepts, cells, sessions, and common analytical workflows.
exam_traps: Treating a Notebook as a replacement for every production orchestration pattern.

skills.title: Create and organize databases, schemas, and tables
skills.objective: Understand the basic Snowflake object hierarchy and create common database objects.
exam_traps: Confusing a schema container with a database or table.

skills.title: Use stages and virtual warehouses
skills.objective: Understand stage locations and the role of virtual warehouses as independent compute resources.
exam_traps: Assuming storage and warehouse compute are the same resource.

skills.title: Load and query structured data
skills.objective: Use basic file formats, stages, COPY patterns, tables, and SQL to load and query structured data.
exam_traps: Confusing file storage with parsing configuration.

skills.title: Work with semi-structured and unstructured data
skills.objective: Recognize VARIANT/semi-structured patterns and Snowflake capabilities for unstructured data.
exam_traps: Assuming all non-tabular content should be converted to relational columns before Snowflake can use it.

skills.title: Understand roles, grants, and least privilege
skills.objective: Use role-based access concepts to understand how users receive privileges in Snowflake.
exam_traps: Granting broad privileges directly to users when a role-based answer is available.

skills.title: Understand access to databases, schemas, and tables
skills.objective: Recognize container and object privileges needed to access Snowflake data.
exam_traps: Forgetting parent-container access in a table access scenario.

skills.title: Understand organization, account, database, schema, and object scope
skills.objective: Recognize Snowflake administrative scopes and where common settings and objects live.
exam_traps: Applying an account-level concept at database or schema scope.

skills.title: Recognize basic account and usage monitoring
skills.objective: Identify common places to inspect account, warehouse, and query activity at an introductory level.
exam_traps: Using an unrelated governance feature to answer an operational monitoring question.

skills.title: Use Snowflake Cortex LLM functions
skills.objective: Recognize common Cortex LLM function use cases and how they operate on Snowflake data.
exam_traps: Confusing a managed Cortex function with deploying a custom model runtime.

skills.title: Match Cortex capabilities to introductory AI use cases
skills.objective: Choose an appropriate Snowflake AI capability for summarization, extraction, classification, and text-generation scenarios.
exam_traps: Choosing a complex custom architecture when a managed Cortex capability directly fits the requirement.

domains.title: Native App Architecture and Best Practices

skills.title: Design application packages and consumer-safe architecture
skills.objective: Understand application packages, installed applications, provider/consumer boundaries, and secure design practices.
exam_traps: Confusing provider-owned package objects with consumer-installed application objects.

skills.title: Design permissions and secure object access
skills.objective: Apply Native App permissions, references, privileges, and secure access patterns without over-privileging consumers or applications.
exam_traps: Assuming an application should automatically receive broad consumer-account privileges.

skills.title: Build setup scripts, manifests, and application objects
skills.objective: Understand setup scripts, manifest configuration, application roles, and object creation during installation or upgrade.
exam_traps: Placing provider-development configuration in the wrong application lifecycle file.

skills.title: Manage versions, patches, release directives, and upgrades
skills.objective: Use Native App versioning and release workflows to safely promote and upgrade applications.
exam_traps: Treating an application version and a release directive as identical concepts.

skills.title: Implement Native App procedures and runtime workflows
skills.objective: Design procedures and application logic that respect provider/consumer execution and security boundaries.
exam_traps: Ignoring execution-rights context in a procedure that touches consumer data.

skills.title: Use references for consumer-owned objects
skills.objective: Use references to let applications interact with consumer-selected objects without requiring unsafe direct ownership patterns.
exam_traps: Hard-coding consumer object access where a reference should be used.

skills.title: Create and manage application billing events
skills.objective: Understand monetization/billing event concepts and how applications report billable usage.
exam_traps: Confusing application billing events with warehouse resource monitors.

skills.title: Monitor Native App cost and operational usage
skills.objective: Design application cost monitoring and observability appropriate to provider and consumer responsibilities.
exam_traps: Assuming provider visibility should expose consumer-sensitive data.

skills.title: Design masking, row access, tagging, and governance controls
skills.objective: Select and combine Snowflake governance controls to meet data protection and privacy requirements.
exam_traps: Using masking to solve row filtering or row access to solve column-value protection.

skills.title: Design secure data lifecycle and protection architecture
skills.objective: Apply encryption, retention, replication, secure sharing, and data-boundary practices to protect sensitive information.
exam_traps: Treating one recovery or encryption feature as a complete governance program.

skills.title: Design advanced RBAC and least-privilege hierarchies
skills.objective: Build scalable role hierarchies, access roles, ownership models, and managed access patterns.
exam_traps: Using powerful system roles for normal workload access.

skills.title: Implement federation, MFA, OAuth, SCIM, and network controls
skills.objective: Choose identity, authentication, provisioning, authorization, and network-origin controls for enterprise scenarios.
exam_traps: Confusing identity lifecycle, interactive authentication, and network restriction controls.

skills.title: Audit access, login, query, and policy activity
skills.objective: Use Snowflake history and Account Usage views to investigate security events and demonstrate control effectiveness.
exam_traps: Choosing a data-protection policy when the requirement is retrospective audit evidence.

skills.title: Map Snowflake controls to regulatory and compliance requirements
skills.objective: Design control evidence, monitoring, retention, and governance to support compliance obligations.
exam_traps: Assuming a platform feature alone replaces organizational control processes and evidence.

skills.title: Assess Snowflake threats, risks, and attack paths
skills.objective: Identify risky identities, privilege escalation, exposed integrations, abnormal access, and data-exfiltration paths.
exam_traps: Focusing only on SQL injection-style threats while ignoring cloud identity and privilege paths.

skills.title: Execute security incident containment and investigation
skills.objective: Prioritize containment, credential/token response, evidence preservation, investigation, and recovery in Snowflake incidents.
exam_traps: Destroying evidence or broadening privileges before containment and investigation are understood.

skills.title: Use Snowflake AI/ML capabilities for security detection and analysis
skills.objective: Apply Snowflake AI/ML and analytical capabilities to identify anomalies, classify data, and accelerate security analysis.
exam_traps: Using Gen AI output as an unverified enforcement decision without governance or deterministic controls.

skills.title: Secure AI and model-enabled security workflows
skills.objective: Apply access, data, prompt/output, and model governance to AI-assisted security workflows.
exam_traps: Sending sensitive information to an AI workflow without checking data and access boundaries.

skills.title: Frame data science problems and choose evaluation methods
skills.objective: Translate business questions into supervised, unsupervised, forecasting, or Gen AI problem formulations and appropriate evaluation metrics.
exam_traps: Choosing a metric that does not reflect the business cost or class distribution.

skills.title: Design reproducible experiments and model comparisons
skills.objective: Apply train/validation/test, cross-validation, leakage prevention, and reproducibility concepts in Snowflake workflows.
exam_traps: Evaluating a model on data that leaked target or future information.

skills.title: Build scalable Snowpark-based data science workflows
skills.objective: Use Snowpark and Snowflake compute appropriately for feature preparation, training, and scoring workloads.
exam_traps: Pulling large datasets client-side when the transformation can execute in Snowflake.

skills.title: Apply reproducibility, lineage, and governance to ML workflows
skills.objective: Track data, feature, model, metric, and deployment context for governed production data science.
exam_traps: Treating a successful notebook run as sufficient production model governance.

skills.title: Prepare data and engineer reliable features
skills.objective: Transform, encode, scale, aggregate, and validate model features using Snowflake-native workflows.
exam_traps: Applying transformations inconsistently between training and inference.

skills.title: Design reusable governed feature pipelines
skills.objective: Create reusable, point-in-time-safe feature datasets with suitable refresh and lineage behavior.
exam_traps: Creating training features using data that would not have been available at prediction time.

skills.title: Train, tune, and evaluate machine learning models
skills.objective: Use appropriate Snowflake/Snowpark ML training, tuning, metrics, and comparison techniques.
exam_traps: Selecting a model solely by training score without validation evidence.

skills.title: Register, version, and use models for inference
skills.objective: Use Snowflake Model Registry and governed inference patterns for batch or production model use.
exam_traps: Deploying an unversioned model without reproducible feature and dependency context.

skills.title: Use Cortex AI and LLM capabilities in data science solutions
skills.objective: Choose managed Cortex AI/LLM capabilities for text, retrieval, extraction, and generation use cases.
exam_traps: Building custom infrastructure when a managed Snowflake AI service directly meets the requirement.

skills.title: Evaluate and govern Gen AI outputs
skills.objective: Design evaluation, grounding, guardrail, cost, and quality controls for production Gen AI workflows.
exam_traps: Using subjective spot checks as the only production LLM quality control.

skills.title: Administer accounts, users, roles, integrations, and account parameters
skills.objective: Manage Snowflake account objects, identity lifecycle, role delegation, integrations, and administrative settings.
exam_traps: Performing routine administration with a broader system role than required.

skills.title: Operate governance and security controls
skills.objective: Administer access, policies, tags, classification, authentication, and audit controls across Snowflake.
exam_traps: Treating monitoring, authentication, and data protection as interchangeable control layers.

skills.title: Manage database and schema objects at scale
skills.objective: Create, alter, clone, recover, transfer ownership, and manage lifecycle of core Snowflake objects.
exam_traps: Applying object-level operations without considering ownership and dependent grants.

skills.title: Operate warehouses, scaling, resource monitors, and workload isolation
skills.objective: Configure warehouse sizing, auto-suspend/resume, multi-cluster behavior, workload isolation, and cost guardrails.
exam_traps: Using resize to solve concurrency or multi-cluster to solve a single slow query without evidence.

skills.title: Monitor query, warehouse, storage, and account activity
skills.objective: Use Snowsight, Information Schema, Account Usage, alerts, and histories to operate Snowflake proactively.
exam_traps: Using a delayed historical source for a requirement that needs near-current troubleshooting without considering latency.

skills.title: Tune platform performance and cost
skills.objective: Diagnose query/warehouse/storage cost and choose evidence-based tuning actions.
exam_traps: Scaling compute before identifying pruning, queueing, spill, or cache behavior.

skills.title: Administer shares, listings, and provider/consumer access
skills.objective: Create and govern secure data sharing and listing relationships across accounts.
exam_traps: Building data-copy pipelines when secure sharing directly fits the requirement.

skills.title: Operate reader accounts and Marketplace consumption
skills.objective: Understand reader-account responsibilities, Marketplace/listing access, and consumption governance.
exam_traps: Assuming reader-account compute/cost responsibility is identical to a normal independent consumer account.

skills.title: Operate Time Travel, Fail-safe, and object recovery
skills.objective: Use retention, UNDROP, historical access, and recovery features appropriately while understanding their limits.
exam_traps: Using Fail-safe as a routine user-accessible backup mechanism.

skills.title: Design and operate replication and failover
skills.objective: Configure and reason about account/database replication, failover groups, RPO/RTO, and recovery procedures.
exam_traps: Treating Time Travel alone as a cross-region disaster-recovery strategy.

skills.title: Load and validate analytical data
skills.objective: Use stages, file formats, COPY, validation, and basic ingestion patterns to prepare analytical datasets.
exam_traps: Confusing where files are stored with how they are parsed.

skills.title: Inspect and clean analytical inputs
skills.objective: Profile nulls, duplicates, types, ranges, and data quality before downstream analysis.
exam_traps: Jumping into advanced analysis before validating the analytical grain and quality.

skills.title: Build reliable SQL transformations
skills.objective: Use joins, aggregations, window functions, CTEs, conditional logic, and set operations to create analytical data.
exam_traps: Using the wrong grain or join cardinality and silently duplicating measures.

skills.title: Transform semi-structured analytical data
skills.objective: Navigate VARIANT data, cast values, and use FLATTEN to create relational analytical shapes.
exam_traps: Flattening at the wrong nesting level and multiplying rows unexpectedly.

skills.title: Build complex analytical queries
skills.objective: Compose advanced Snowflake SQL with windows, pivots, recursive/complex CTEs, date logic, and analytical patterns.
exam_traps: Using WHERE when QUALIFY is required to filter results after window evaluation.

skills.title: Troubleshoot analytical query correctness and performance
skills.objective: Diagnose logical errors, join explosions, filters, query plans, pruning, and compute issues in analytical SQL.
exam_traps: Treating a correctness issue as a warehouse-size problem.

skills.title: Choose Snowflake built-in functions for analytical problems
skills.objective: Use date/time, string, conversion, conditional, statistical, and semi-structured functions effectively.
exam_traps: Creating custom logic when a simpler built-in function already provides the required semantics.

skills.title: Create and use UDFs appropriately
skills.objective: Recognize when a UDF is appropriate and understand scalar/table function boundaries and maintainability tradeoffs.
exam_traps: Using a UDF where standard SQL or a built-in function is clearer and easier to optimize.

skills.title: Perform descriptive analysis and segmentation
skills.objective: Summarize distributions, cohorts, trends, outliers, and categorical/continuous measures using Snowflake SQL.
exam_traps: Using averages without considering skew, outliers, or analytical grain.

skills.title: Perform diagnostic analysis to explain observed changes
skills.objective: Use drill-downs, comparisons, cohorts, contribution analysis, and dimensional slicing to investigate why metrics changed.
exam_traps: Confusing correlation from a diagnostic slice with causal proof.

skills.title: Use forecasting and predictive analytical capabilities
skills.objective: Recognize suitable predictive/forecasting approaches and interpret outputs for business analysis.
exam_traps: Evaluating a time-series model with a split that leaks future information.

skills.title: Use Snowflake AI capabilities in analytical workflows
skills.objective: Apply managed Snowflake AI/LLM functions where they add analytical value while controlling evaluation and cost.
exam_traps: Using free-form generation where a deterministic analytical function is required.

skills.title: Prepare governed datasets for business consumption
skills.objective: Design analytical outputs with the correct grain, semantics, security, freshness, and performance for consumers.
exam_traps: Exposing a convenient dataset without preserving governance or metric definitions.

skills.title: Communicate analytical results and limitations
skills.objective: Present findings with appropriate context, uncertainty, definitions, filters, and reproducible business logic.
exam_traps: Presenting a metric without documenting population, time window, or grain.
